title: Question 3
stem:
To demonstrate simple harmonic motion, a student attaches a trolley to two similar stretched
springs, as shown in Fig. 3.1.
The trolley has mass m of 810 g.
The trolley is displaced along the line of the two springs and then released. The subsequent
acceleration a of the trolley is given by the expression
a = -(2k x)/(m)
where the spring constant k for each of the springs is 64 N m^{-1} and x is the displacement of the
trolley.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the frequency of oscillation of the trolley is 2.0 Hz.
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in simple harmonic motion connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: 2k/m = ω2; ω = 2πf; (2 × 64 / 0.810) = (2π × f)2 leading to f = 2.0 Hz
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Simple harmonic motion. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
2k/m = ω2; ω = 2πf; (2 × 64 / 0.810) = (2π × f)2 leading to f = 2.0 Hz
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The maximum displacement of the trolley is 1.6 cm.
Calculate the maximum speed of the trolley.

markscheme_points.text: v0 = ωx0 or v0 = 2πfx0 or v = ω(x0 2 - x2)1/2 and x = 0

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

Suggest the change, if any, that occurs in the frequency and in the maximum speed of the
